quotes.name: Priya
quotes.q: The prep sheet gets vegetarian right most of the time, but then the menu my kids are reading says pork and the double feature wants me to buy lamb. And there's egg in almost everything, so I'm still checking every line myself.
quotes.pay: maybe, a few dollars once if egg-free and no-beef filters worked everywhere
quotes.gave_up: Double feature shopping list listed 2kg lamb shoulder with Vegetarian on

quotes.name: Yusuf
quotes.q: It's a great idea for the cousins but every film I tried had pork in it. If I have to go through every dish myself I may as well just order pizza.
quotes.pay: no, not until there's a halal setting
quotes.gave_up: Pork in all four films with no way to remove it except going fully vegetarian

quotes.name: Miriam
quotes.q: It looks beautiful and the films are the ones we love, but nearly every menu mixes meat and milk or has lobster in it. I'd be rewriting dinner from scratch.
quotes.pay: no
quotes.gave_up: Meat and dairy combined in the same dish (Casablanca briouats brushed with butter) and shellfish mains

quotes.name: Harjit
quotes.q: Veg and no alcohol together actually worked on the prep sheet, which surprised me. I just wish the printed menu matched and there was one Hindi film in there for my nani.
quotes.pay: maybe, small one-off for a family pack with Indian films

quotes.name: Raj
quotes.q: The engine is clearly there because Vegetarian swaps every dish. Give me a 'no beef' switch and a 'one veg plate' option and I'd use it every week.
quotes.pay: maybe, if it had ingredient exclusions and mixed menus
quotes.gave_up: Could not build a menu that is half vegetarian and beef-free

quotes.name: Ruth
quotes.q: Outside Lent I'd use this, the Mamma Mia menu is lovely. But we fast a lot of the year and every vegetarian menu is full of feta and eggs.
quotes.pay: maybe, if a fasting mode existed
quotes.gave_up: Every vegetarian menu built on cheese, butter and eggs

quotes.name: Arjun
quotes.q: I didn't expect Jain support, and there isn't any. Onions, garlic or potatoes in every menu I tried. The data's structured enough that an ingredient exclude list wouldn't be hard.
quotes.pay: no
quotes.gave_up: First shopping list (Toy Story: 1kg baby potatoes, chives, 4 eggs)

quotes.name: Linh
quotes.q: Honestly the video store and candy bar are the fun bit, we'd use those every week. But I need to know if dinner is $20 or $80 before I send it to the group chat.
quotes.pay: maybe, a one-off $2 to $3 if it had a cheap mode and a cost estimate

quotes.name: Grace
quotes.q: I've got a kettle and a microwave that smells like popcorn already. Love the look, but Lazy night still wants me to grill corn.
quotes.pay: no
quotes.gave_up: Cooking: every Lazy night menu I got still needed a stove, grill or oven, so I fell back to buying lollies from the Candy bar

quotes.name: Chloe
quotes.q: It's so cute I'd post it, but the save gives me a square with tiny writing. Give me a story-sized one with the poster and I'm sold.
quotes.pay: maybe, $2 to $4 for story templates and themed packs

quotes.name: Ahmed
quotes.q: No alcohol is done properly, I'll give it that. But no halal option and bacon in the sandwich means I'm checking every recipe myself.
quotes.pay: no

quotes.name: Fatima
quotes.q: The candy bar is the best bit, but half those lollies have gelatine and it doesn't say. I'd still have to read every packet.
quotes.pay: no

quotes.name: Isaac
quotes.q: Cool once, then I want it in under three seconds. And a movie app with no Mario or Sonic is missing my whole crowd.
quotes.pay: no, unless it adds a gaming aisle and instant mode

quotes.name: Leo
quotes.q: The food's legit, sweetbreads for the boys is a flex. Just give me the steps one line at a time in a normal font, those fancy numbers mess with me.
quotes.pay: yes, $5 one-off for a chef mode with a run sheet and step timers

quotes.name: Aunty Rose
quotes.q: The kids would go mad for the wheel and the lollies. But I pressed back and the whole thing disappeared on me, and that little menu I can't read without my glasses and even then.
quotes.pay: no, but would happily use it free for school holidays

quotes.name: Bazza
quotes.q: Spun it, got a film, fair enough. Then it wants me to make shrimp cocktail and a michelada. Give me the chops and veg and I'm happy.
quotes.pay: no

quotes.name: Doug
quotes.q: I typed Singing in the Rain and it told me there was no such film. Then I found Casablanca and the screen jumped to a picture of a picture theatre and I thought I'd broken it.
quotes.pay: no

quotes.name: Pat
quotes.q: The bits with big gold buttons I can manage. The actual menu, the part I came for, is like reading the fine print on a pill bottle.
quotes.pay: no
quotes.gave_up: Reading the printed menu on the phone; dish names are a few pixels high and tapping does not enlarge them

quotes.name: Bev
quotes.q: Once I found it, it was the prettiest menu I have ever seen and I'll put it on the table. Getting there took me three goes and a grandson would have helped.
quotes.pay: maybe, a few dollars for printable menu packs for themed afternoons

quotes.name: Nadia
quotes.q: I tick no alcohol and the menu still says vodka. Then in the other tab it is okay. I need it to say halal, and to say it in easy words.
quotes.pay: no

quotes.name: Tanvir
quotes.q: Half a minute to open, another half a minute for the wheel. My kids are already fighting by then. And still no halal button.
quotes.pay: no

quotes.name: Sam
quotes.q: The bones are better than most sites. Search, the prep sheet headings and labelled buttons all work. But I spun the wheel and my phone went silent, so I had no idea what film I'd landed on.
quotes.pay: no, not until spin results are announced and recipes read properly; maybe a few dollars after that

quotes.name: Jordan
quotes.q: This is the most fun I've seen in a recipe app, the menus feel like real props. It just needs to stop opening on a ghost Ghostbusters and to show me something when I tap a tab.
quotes.pay: maybe, $5 to 10 one-off for printable menu packs or a party kit; not a subscription

quotes.name: Kate
quotes.q: The content is the product here, 850 bespoke menus is a lot of work and it shows. What's missing is the boring stuff: a clear first step, a privacy page and a way to get the shopping list onto my phone.
quotes.pay: maybe: $4 to 6 one-off or about $15 a year for sync, holiday party packs and shopping list export; would not pay for the core spin

quotes.name: Lisa
quotes.q: It's actually very tidy, nothing is tracked and it all stays on my computer. But the minute it offers to put my card online with a four digit PIN, I want to know where it's going, and nothing tells me.
quotes.pay: no for the app itself; maybe a small amount for sync if it explained where data lives and let me delete it
quotes.gave_up: Put my card online: could not find out what gets uploaded, where to, or how to delete it

quotes.name: Dave
quotes.q: The years are spot on and the marathon menu idea is a beauty. But don't tell me Alien is part 1 of 2, and you can't go from Rocky IV straight to Creed.
quotes.pay: no; maybe $5 if the series were complete and the marathons had running times

quotes.name: Marco
quotes.q: Whoever wrote these methods can cook, the temperatures are right and the make-ahead notes are gold. But give me an ingredient list per dish, and don't tell me chilling a can of Coke is four hours of cooking.
quotes.pay: maybe: $5 to 10 for proper per-dish recipe cards and a reliable scaler for a big family; not for the current format

quotes.name: Sione
quotes.q: Mate, it's beautiful and the youth will love the wheel, but when I set 20 people and the double feature still says serves 4, I'm back doing maths on the back of the church bulletin.
quotes.pay: maybe, a few dollars a year if crowd sizes actually flow through everything
quotes.gave_up: Double feature shopping list still says serves 4 for a youth group of 20

quotes.name: Marisol
quotes.q: I turned on lazy night and it gave me marmalade sandwiches and a cocoa. That's not dinner, love, that's what I eat at 3am on night shift.
quotes.pay: no
quotes.gave_up: Lazy night gave snacks and a drink, not dinner, and did nothing on Home Alone

quotes.name: Shona
quotes.q: The candy bar is pure magic, my two would spend an hour in it. I just need to know it won't cost me sixty quid before I start.
quotes.pay: maybe, small one-off for a kids pack

quotes.name: Amara
quotes.q: Locking in Moana for Saturday at six is exactly how my house runs. Now tell me what time to start cooking and I'm sold.
quotes.pay: yes, a few dollars a month for timelines and calendar reminders

quotes.name: Emma
quotes.q: It's gorgeous, but the first family film I opened was E.T. and it's peanut butter three ways with no warning. I can't hand this to my husband to cook from.
quotes.pay: maybe, if allergens were properly flagged, I'd pay for that peace of mind
quotes.gave_up: No nut filter or warnings; E.T. menu is peanut butter end to end

quotes.name: Tui
quotes.q: I cook for 400 kids a day so I know a scaled list when I see one. Good bones, but nobody buys 20 tablespoons of flour and nobody's buying 10 lamb racks for a movie night.
quotes.pay: maybe, if it did proper crowd quantities and costs

quotes.name: Noah
quotes.q: Spin button's perfect one-handed. Then it tells me to start cooking yesterday. Lazy night needs to mean actual dinner with zero effort, not a cocktail.
quotes.pay: no
quotes.gave_up: Lazy night left a knish snack and a whisky sour, no actual dinner

quotes.name: Wei
quotes.q: The prep sheet is better than most recipe sites, and the make-ahead notes are gold. But if you know my showtime and every step's minutes, just tell me what time to start the sauce.
quotes.pay: maybe, a few dollars once for a run sheet and method that scales properly

quotes.name: Jake and Tom
quotes.q: It's gorgeous and I'd print the menu for the table in a heartbeat, but Tom can't eat four of the five dishes and the app doesn't even tell you that. Give me a gluten free toggle and I'm in.
quotes.pay: maybe, would pay for proper allergen filters
quotes.gave_up: Checking the Godfather menu for Tom: 4 of 5 dishes need wheat and there is no gluten free option or swap

quotes.name: Kirra
quotes.q: I ticked vegetarian and the menu card still says sirloin. Then the actual recipes are full of butter, eggs and honey. Pretty app, not for me.
quotes.pay: no
quotes.gave_up: Reading the vegetarian Valentine's Day list: goat's cheese, cream cheese, 245g butter, eggs, buttermilk, honey

quotes.name: Hemi
quotes.q: Easy enough on the phone and the kids would love the candy bar. Just let me pick a Tuesday, I'm not home most weekends.
quotes.pay: maybe, small one-off to plan a whole week home

quotes.name: Hannah
quotes.q: My kids would love this, but I had to Google 175C and figure out what 400 grams of butter is in sticks. One units switch and it's perfect.
quotes.pay: maybe, for a US units mode

quotes.name: Mei
quotes.q: Very beautiful, my grandson would like Nemo. But I cannot have the dairy and the small words are hard for me to read.
quotes.pay: no
quotes.gave_up: Lock in: earliest showtime is 5pm and the dishes need dairy swaps she has to work out herself

quotes.name: Steph
quotes.q: The Halloween menu is so good I want to frame it. But I can't build my own marathon and Scream has no sequels, which is wild for a horror night.
quotes.pay: maybe, for custom marathons with a combined shopping list
quotes.gave_up: Trying to build a 4 film Halloween horror marathon of her own picks
